Files, browser drafts & troubleshooting

Save project includes waveLAB, beatMAP, melodyLAB, continuityLAB, waveforms and patterns. Secret WOOFpad history stays private. Individual lab saves still work.

A browser draft is a convenience, not your only copy. Save a project file before closing or switching browsers. Downloads may appear in your browser’s Downloads list. Loading is silent; Open replaces the working project and offers Undo project open.

No sound? Press Play, check MASTER, and try Test sound in continuityLAB. If an embedded browser blocks microphones or downloads, use the downloadable HTML edition in a desktop browser. Imported audio in the song is limited to 60 seconds total. MIDI exports notes; WAV keeps your exact sounds.

◖ Room tune Hear your room · adjust your speakers
A little sound check for your listening spot.

Use speakers, put your microphone where you sit, and keep the room quiet. The seven-second test pauses studio playback, makes a soft rising sweep, then listens to its tail. Start with low speaker volume.

Ready. No microphone opens until you start the test.
Measured tail
Suggested speaker EQ · cuts only

Approximate speaker + microphone + room response at this spot, not a calibrated measurement. EQ can soften prominent frequencies; it cannot remove wall reflections. Room tune affects studio listening only, before the safety limiter. Songs and exports stay unchanged. Browser speech and YouTube use separate audio paths. Measure again after moving speakers or switching rooms. Microphone audio stays local and is discarded after analysis.

☎ Landline calling EXPERIMENTAL BETAHardware setup required

Real calls need your own equipment. Supply an active telephone line, an FXO telephone-line gateway, and a WebRTC calling server. This beta has not been tested on a real landline. A plain cable or an FXS-only adapter will not connect the studio to a wall jack.

DOT WAVE → YOUR CALLING SERVER → FXO GATEWAY → ACTIVE WALL LINE
Setup & beta test notes
  1. Test the wall jack with a regular telephone first. Use a telephone-line gateway's FXO / LINE port, following its manual. Never connect a phone line to a computer audio jack.
  2. Ask your server administrator for a secure WebSocket address, SIP identity and account login. The server must support browser audio and route this account through your FXO gateway. Asterisk with WebRTC support is one option.
  3. Enter those details below, then Connect. Registration checks the account; it does not prove the telephone line works.
  4. With a headset, make a short call to a willing tester. Check audio both ways, mute, keypad tones and hangup. Confirm the line is free afterward.

No emergency calling support. Line charges may apply. Incoming calls, call transfers and automatic redial are disabled. Your server/provider handles real call routing and may keep call records.

The login and dialed number stay in this page's memory, outside song saves. Disconnect clears password fields. No built-in call recording. Call audio bypasses the studio effects, Room tune and safety limiter; Master still scales listening volume. Use a comfortable headset level.

Stop all, Escape, starting another microphone tool, hiding this browser tab, or leaving the page ends the call. Switching studio labs keeps the floating call controls available. If the connection fails, confirm hangup on your gateway or regular telephone.

Calling server setup · Example FXO gateway manual · Full notes in LANDLINE-BETA-GUIDE.txt in the download.

Optional network relay Only if your administrator supplies one

No public relay is used by default. Remote servers may need TURN for two-way audio.

▣ ROM & SOUNDFONT SOUNDS SNES first · local files

Open a SNES ROM, SPC sound snapshot, SF2 bank or ZIP. Preview a sample, then snip it into a waveform for the labs.

SNES .sfc / .smc · .spc · uncompressed .sf2 · ZIP. Files up to 64 MB; ZIPs up to 128 MB. Nothing is uploaded.

No bank loaded
Preview → name → snip → save waveform
Console support & getting the right file

ZIP: one matching file opens automatically; choose a file when there are several. Standard stored and DEFLATE ZIPs are supported, including files inside folders. Password-protected, split and ZIP64 archives need to be extracted first. ZIP contents use the same console support below.

SNES: direct ROM scans look for uncompressed BRR samples. Results can include false matches and can miss compressed samples. An SPC snapshot from an emulator provides a sample directory for the current song. Sounds are previewed at 32 kHz; the original instrument pitch is not known.

GBA, N64, NES & Genesis: direct ROM extraction is not implemented yet. Open their extracted SF2 samples here, or use Open audio in Capture for a WAV. NES and Genesis sounds often require rendering chip instruments rather than copying a sample bank.

SoundFonts: this imports raw PCM samples, not complete presets, velocity layers, envelopes or modulation. Saving a snip creates a repeating studio waveform. The original sample stays available in Capture while this page is open.

Extraction tools: VGMTrans for supported SNES/GBA music formats; N64 tools for supported N64 games. Compatibility depends on each game's sound engine.

♬ Guitar chord pocket 16 shapes · standard tuning

Strings run low E → high E. × = mute, ○ = open. Dot numbers are fingers: 1 index, 2 middle, 3 ring, 4 pinky. Thick green lines are barres.

C
Plays the guitar’s actual pitches with the Chords part’s sound.
How the chord pocket works

Major and natural minor scales each use seven notes. Chords stack selected notes together; the piano cards show nine chord types for any root. The circle connects keys a fifth apart, while the inner ring shows their relative minors. Piano labels show sounding pitches; the note list keeps each chord’s musical spelling.

Browser speech uses a separate audio path. Its level includes Master; changing level may repeat the current phrase. Studio effects, Safe Mode’s limiter, and music WAV exports do not include it.

Voices & saved files

The voice list comes from your browser and device. Local voices are shown first. If none appear, press Refresh or open this studio in a desktop browser with installed speech voices. Some voices may ignore pitch, pause, or other controls.

Save voice preset keeps your text, selected voice, and settings in a separate file. Open text / preset accepts that file or plain .txt. Presets never start speaking automatically or enable online voices by themselves. These files are separate from music projects.

Speech can continue while you use another lab; the floating mixer and Stop All can stop it. Hiding the browser page stops it too. Native browser speech does not provide audio samples for WAV export or the song timeline.
